title: Ealing Community Equipment
description:
London Borough of Ealing has a awarded a contract for Community Equipment from 1st April 2023 for a period of five (5) years with a two (2) year extension option to NOTTINGHAM REHAB LIMITED (TRADING AS NRS HEALTHCARE).

The London Consortium has established a Framework for purchase of Community Equipment and services. Following a tender exercise a Framework Agreement was entered into between the Contracting Authority and Westminster Council by 1st April 2023. London Borough of Ealing is a member of the Consortium.

The Call Off contract from the Framework Agreement is between London Borough of Ealing and NOTTINGHAM REHAB LIMITED (TRADING AS NRS HEALTHCARE). It includes a local contract between NRS Healthcare and LBE for the provision of Telecare equipment and minor adaptations. The total value over 5 years is estimated as 16.5m GBP

The contract allows London borough of Ealing to purchase Community Equipment. Community Equipment services provide equipment and small adaptations to support people living at home. Examples are riser/recliner chairs, bathroom and toilet adaptions and aids, pressure mattresses and sensory aids. The service is available to all Ealing residents who are assessed by social care and NHS professionals as needing it, including children.

People using the service may be older adults, people with physical disabilities, sensory impairment or long term health conditions, or people who are autistic and/or have a learning disabilities. As well as supporting people to live independently at home, community equipment can reduce the need for care and support and delay the need for more intensive support or treatment. Community equipment can reduce falls which can lead to hospital admission and support timely discharge from hospital when a person is recovering.

title: Severe Mental Illness - Health Check, Vaccination and Screening Ealing
description:
The NHS NW London ICB required the provision of Severe Mental Illness (SMI) Outreach Engagement Services in Ealing.

Individuals living with SMI are often difficult to engage with for health checks and ongoing treatment, with high dropout or DNA rates. Poor engagement may lead to worse clinical outcomes, with symptom relapse and potential hospitalisation. Numerous variables may affect level of treatment engagement, including accessibility of care, and a patient's trust that the treatment will address his/her own unique goals.

Providing person‐centred care, including shared decision making, is an approach that focuses on an individual's unique goals and life circumstances. Use of person‐centred care in mental health treatment models has promising outcomes for engagement. Particular populations of people have historically been difficult to engage, such as people from black and minority ethnic groups, young adults experiencing a first episode of psychosis, individuals with coexisting psychotic and substance use disorders, and those who are homeless.

This contract was awarded to CAPE (Community Activities Project Ealing) via a Below Threshold quoting exercise.

title: Foster with West London Digital Marketing 2025/26
description:
The London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham ('the Council') invited Quotations for the support of digital advertising services to recruit foster carers across eight North West London Local Authorities ('the Contract'). Operational from May 2024, the London Boroughs of London Borough of  Hammersmith & Fulham (lead Local Authority), Brent, Ealing, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster City Council have joined together to form 'Foster with West London', a collaborative partnership working together to recruit foster carers who can provide a loving and safe home to children in care in west London. Hammersmith & Fulham sought to appoint a digital marketing agency to plan and deliver a digital campaign for 2025/26 to increase the number of foster carers across North West London. The campaign should continue to effectively reach and engage potential foster carers through awareness raising activity, educating them about the process and benefits of fostering, and encouraging them to apply, and engaging those actively considering fostering. Alongside this, the successful Supplier shall also work with the 'Foster with West London' team to develop and implement strategies to increase the conversion to approved foster carers across the region.  
The primary target audience for this campaign should be individuals or families who meet the eligibility criteria for becoming foster carers with particular focus on those living within the eight North West London Local Authorities or neighbouring areas.

title: Provision of Health and Safety Advisor Services
description:
West London Waste (WLWA) is a statutory Waste Disposal Authority (WDA) formed in 1986. WLWA is responsible for disposing of waste collected by the London Boroughs of Brent, Ealing, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow and Richmond upon Thames. About 1.7 million people live in this area, which covers 38,000 hectares. 

West London Waste Authority is looking to appoint Health & Safety (H&S) Advisory Services to advise on relevant Health and Safety management issues impacting the organisation.

Service requirements:

To procure Health and Safety consultancy services for WLWA to obtain the external expertise to enhance compliance with regulatory standards, improve workplace safety culture, and reduce incidents of accidents and hazards within waste management operations.
 
The new proposed procurement aims to leverage specialised expertise, provide tailored risk management strategies, and ensure continuous monitoring and improvement of Health and Safety practices while achieving cost efficiencies and supporting sustainable waste management objectives.

In order to achieve this, WLWA will require the awarded H&S consultancy to provide the following services (including but not limited to):
•	Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR) reportable incidents support.
•	Writing new risk assessments.
•	High risk accident reporting support.
•	Annual review of all risk assessments - Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH), fire, site processes.
•	New Contractor Risk Assessment Method Statement  & compliance where required.
•	Quarterly site inspections of our sites.
•	Review of site management plans/permits/licenses' where required.
•	Verification of consultants/supplier credentials  that WLMA may contract with.
•	Support for supplier H&S issues.
•	H&S training as per our request, for example, emergency first aid training, annually. Led or organised by the Consultants.
•	H&S policy updates. Compliance and legislation updates.
•	Consultancy advice on new processes / infrastructure changes or projects.
•	Support for the end to end process in respect of insurance/injury claims from employees.
•	H&S representation in court if required following an injury claim
•	Proactively improve H&S across Sites with Strategic Plans, such as ISO or BS Accreditation. 
•	Construction Design Management. 
•	Using Work Wallet as a platform for KPI's - Management of system, assisting Operations Manager.

To access the ITT and supporting documentation please follow the link below. 

https://westlondonwaste.gov.uk/news/health-safety-tender

title: Further competiton for the provision of e-books
description:
The University of West London (UWL) invites you to submit a bid to supply E-Books to its 
Libraries.
1.1.2 UWL Library Services and Archives is core to the student and academic experience at 
the University of West London, and supports our institutional strategic focus on 
developing learners as innovative and creative professionals.
Our library team support a student body of over 10,000 and 1,000 staff in all aspects of 
library and information provision across two sites with our main Paul Hamlyn Library at 
our Ealing site and a health library at our Reading site. UWL also has a possible 3rd site 
at Ruskin College, Oxford.
Library Services is in the final year of our current strategic plan which runs until 2023. 
Centred within our strategy is developing inclusive, welcoming library services which 
reflect our university's mission of extending higher education to those traditionally 
excluded from it.
Two principles are core to delivery of our plan:
• A continuous improvement approach to service development, which 
alongside year-on-year improvements in customer service has seen us 
create key performance indicators based on new methodologies.
• Main-streaming of user experience (UX) research, which forms an 
important basis for our qualitative understanding of our students' needs and 
expectations of a contemporary library service.
For further information, please visit www.uwl.ac.uk/library
1.1.3 The go live date is ideally August to allow orders to be placed before the academic year 
begins.
1.1.4 The contract will be for 2 years, with the option to extend for a further 2 years in 12-month
increments (+1+1) subject to satisfactory performance and at the discretion of UWL.
 
1.1.5 UWL may appoint the top two scoring suppliers. All orders initially will go to the first 
selected supplier, but if they cannot supply a particular title or supply times/licence options 
do not meet our needs (for example), then orders will be placed with the second selected 
supplier.
1.1.6 The procurement exercise will be carried out in accordance with and subject to the SUPC

title: DPS Transportation Tender
description:
The Contract is for the provision of transportation providers to provide Home to School Transport and Transport for Adult clients both older persons and with learning disabilities and complex needs.
The purpose of this procurement is to establish a DPS for the provision of Transportation Services for Adults, Children, Looked After Children and Young People with Special Educational Needs (SEN).
The term of the contract is for 4 years with the possibility of an optional 3-year extension.
The intention is that the DPS is an entirely electronic process and routes will be awarded to providers on the DPS using reverse E-auction.  There is no guarantee of business / business volumes.      
The Council is seeking a diverse range of Adults, Children, Looked After Children and           Young People's Transportation including cars, MPV's, minibuses, small and large accessible vehicles, larger buses and coaches of all sizes capable of transporting wheelchair users. There is no limit on the number of Service Providers who can be admitted and, additional Service Providers can join the DPS during the term of the DPS, subject to their applications meeting the Qualification requirements.
Joining the DPS
Transportation Providers wishing to join the DPS are required to review and agree the tender documentation and complete the online ITT via Capital E sourcing. A pass or fail (set out in this document) for the Evaluation Criteria must be met/passed before the Provider will be admitted to the DPS. 
The full suite of tender documents are available via the London Borough of Hillingdon&apos;s tender portal www.capitalesourcing.com

title: One to One Executive Coaching
description:
Introduction: 

The University of Derby are currently looking for external coaching organisation(s) with a substantial pool of qualified coaches to provide coaching to Senior Leaders across the organisation, through individual 1-1 executive coaching. 

Scope: 

We have undergone a period of unprecedented change in recent years, not only in our sector but politically, socially and economically, which has created challenges but also many opportunities for our Senior Leadership Teams.  

We are ambitious for our students, our staff and our region, but equally need to be flexible and adaptable to the changing environment in which we operate. What is right for our students today may not be right tomorrow, and getting this right is most important for our future success. Over the next few years, the nature and pace of change is likely to accelerate even further, and the University therefore needs to be in the best possible position to thrive, in what we know will continue to be challenging circumstances. 

We are committed to building our leadership capability and up and coming talent within the organisation.  Therefore, a future development for 2022/23 will be the launch of a leadership and management development provision, supported by competences.  Underpinning this will be 360 reviews and one to one coaching.   

In order to meet these challenges, and as part of our wider internal Coaching and Mentoring Framework, we would like to work with external coaching provider(s) who can support our Senior Leaders through this period of culture change, uncertainty, and complex challenge, so that we may continue to deliver a high-performing culture. 

The nature of the contract would be over a period of 4 years and on a demand-led basis where the coach would be called upon as and when required and matched accordingly. 

Framework:  

We would like to tender for a framework of suppliers (up to 20 suppliers) to join our external 'pool' of executive 1-1 coaches. There will be no guarantee of sessions as they will be held on a demand-led based on staff requirements and appropriate coach/UoD staff member matching. 

The supplier must also have the flexibility to deliver the sessions face to face or virtually (the University platform is Teams). Face to face delivery is preferable, but the supplier must be able to determine an appropriate balance between the two. 

Suppliers will need to register as a prospective supplier on the University of Derby Oracle portal.  User guides and links found here: https://www.derby.ac.uk/services/finance/procurement-suppliers-and-tendering/supplier-info/prospective-suppliers/

Once registered the supplier will need to access the tender on the Oracle portal.  User guides and links found here: https://www.derby.ac.uk/services/finance/procurement-suppliers-and-tendering/supplier-info/existing-suppliers/
